body.statement: For arbitrary finite \(T,K,q\), can the projection of \(\{\mathbb E_D[\Phi_T\Phi_T^{\top}]:D\in\mathfrak D_T\}\) relevant to \(\mathbb E_D[u_Tu_T^{\top}]\) be characterized by a lag-sized necessary-and-sufficient family of parity and positivity inequalities with explicit sign-orbit recovery?
body.justification: This now isolates only the genuinely unresolved lag-sized finite realizability problem.
body.gap: Pseudomoment positivity and lag-one parity do not characterize genuine binary-law fourth moments at arbitrary lag order.
body.consumer: A lag-sized certificate would avoid enumerating \(2^{T-1}\) sign orbits in exact multi-lag design optimization.

obligation.what_is_open: A necessary-and-sufficient parity and positivity description of the genuine finite binary fourth-moment projection whose size is controlled by the lag order, together with constructive recovery of sign-orbit weights.
obligation.obstruction: Positive semidefiniteness and the lag-one parity inequalities do not characterize the general correlation polytope.  The exact orbit program has exponentially many weights, and the quantitative Golay argument controls the minimax value without recovering every feasible finite projected tensor.
obligation.attempted: Reduced the feasible body exactly to global-sign orbit weights, epigraphed the risk as a finite semidefinite program, checked the scalar parity collapse at one lag, and used endpoint-local Golay covariance to prove the formerly open finite-horizon rate.  None of these steps eliminates the exponential orbit variables for arbitrary lag order.
obligation.partial_result:
The exact orbit formulation in \(\textnormal{prop:finite-orbit-sdp-characterization}\) gives a computable necessary-and-sufficient description with \(2^{T-1}\) weights.  The lag-one parity certificate collapses that program to one scalar moment.  Separately, \(\textnormal{thm:balanced-stationary-golay-optimum-quantitative}\) proves the formerly requested rate
\[
\left|V_{T,K}(q;R_g,R_e)-R_e^2N_q^2\right|
\le \frac{c(K,q,R_g,R_e)}{T}
\]
for fixed \(K,q,R_g,R_e\).  Thus only a lag-sized necessary-and-sufficient finite realizability description and constructive sign-orbit recovery remain open.
